— Tutorial—	MOCK CLAT 10028 : ANSWER & EXPLANATIONS
MOCK CLAT 10028 (ESSENTIAL)
ANSWER & EXPLANATIONS
English Language
1.	Answer: A
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: "Then there is the whole corpus of texts by a group of philosophers
known as the Neo-Pythagoreans... The home, it turns out, was a topic of considerable philosophical
interest in antiquity.”
Why A is correct: The text builds an overarching argument that domestic life was a significant
topic of ancient philosophical inquiry across multiple traditions (Xenophon, Stoics, Neo-
Pythagoreans).
Why others are wrong: B mistakes a modern archival challenge for an ancient historical
constraint.
Cis textually false; Musonius explicitly includes child rearing in his definition of marriage.
D introduces an unsupported claim regarding "redefining legal rights."
2.	Answer: B
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: "...they are philosophical texts written in antiquity, and they are
about the home, and I suspect that, if the home was regarded as a topic worthy of philosophical
interests, they would be read today.”
Why B is correct: The author introduces minor, neglected, or specific Stoic works to prove the
breadth and legitimacy of domestic philosophy in the ancient world.
Why others are wrong: A overemphasizes modern text verification methods. C invents a non-
existent contrast between Greek and Roman educational views. D mistakenly claims the author
maps out a long-term evolutionary timeline.
3.	Answer: A
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: "These texts are commonly rejected by studies of ancient
philosophers because they are hard to date, and quite likely written by writers using pseudonyms."
Why A is correct: The author explicitly attributes the rejection of Neo-Pythagorean domestic
writings to difficulties in verifying their date ("chronological origin") and author authenticity
("pseudonyms").
Why others are wrong: B is incorrect because Musonius originally gained modern fame for his
educational essays, not his domestic ones. C is directly disproven by the three secondary books
cited. D is wrong because the text indicates domestic ethics were deeply tied to macro-politics (e.g.,
ruling a state).
4.	Answer: B
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: "Musonius Rufus had his 15 minutes of fame some 25 years ago
when Martha Nussbaum noticed that he recommended women be educated as well as men. But
while education does matter... so does the home..."

LAW PREP
— Tutorial—	MOCK CLAT 10028 : ANSWER & EXPLANATIONS
Why B is correct: The modern idiom "15 minutes of fame" is integrated into the text to signal a
brief, initial burst of academic interest in Musonius' views on education before scholars expanded
their view to analyze his thoughts on domestic life.
Why others are wrong: A inaccurately claims his baseline authority was undermined. C
attributes a mocking tone toward research institutes that the author does not exhibit. D
misidentifies the phrase as a metaphor for cyclical curricula.
5.	Answer: B
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: (The overall linear structure: Paras 1 & 2 establish the timeline of
the ancient world and the topic; Para 2 addresses modern rejection criteria; Para 3 details
Musonius’ moral parameters of marriage).
Why B is correct: These four terms flawlessly track the conceptual building blocks of the passage
in order: the era, the core discipline, the archival challenges with texts, and the final philosophical
definition of marriage.
Why others are wrong: A overextends "Institutional Bias." C mentions "Stoic Asceticism"
(severe self-denial), which directly contradicts Musonius' emphasis on material and emotional
sharing. D focuses heavily on legal structures ("Jurisprudence") instead of the text's actual focus
on moral philosophy.
6.	Answer: B
Level: Easy
Explanation: Reference Line: “As well as sharing their material possessions, they must share
affection: there should be ‘above all perfect companionship and mutual love of husband and wife’. If
these conditions fail to obtain, ‘the union is doomed to disaster...”
Why B is correct: In formal philosophical language, the intransitive verb "obtain" means to be
established, true, or currently operational. In this context, if the conditions of love and
companionship fail to exist or prevail, the relationship deteriorates.
Why others are wrong: A is the everyday transitive definition ("to acquire something"), which is
grammatically impossible here. C shifts the meaning to durability over long stretches of time. D
describes active functionality rather than the simple presence or baseline truth of the conditions.
7.	Answer: A
Level: Moderate
Explanation: Reference Line: "Though I was raised materially as middle class, my own identity
has had influxes from both extremes of the class circumstances into which my parents were born..."
Why A is correct: The passage focuses on the author's internal processing of wealth, explaining
how their identity was shaped simultaneously by the privilege of their mother's billionaire family
and the industrious, bootstrapping background of their father's family.
Why others are wrong:
B overextends a childhood metric (house size) into a universal structural barrier to identity
formation.
C focuses too heavily on the grandfather, missing the author's broader personal identity synthesis.
D reverses the chronological order of the author's schooling and invents an unmentioned narrative
about financial discipline.

LAW PREP
— Tutorial—	MOCK CLAT 10028 : ANSWER & EXPLANATIONS
Answer: C
Level: Easy
Explanation: Reference Line: "Wealth was always something I quietly wrestled with... my own
identity has had influxes from both extremes of the class circumstances into which my parents were
born..."
Why C is correct: The author uses personal anecdotes—such as shifting school environments and
memories of a wealthy grandfather—to introspectively explore how an awareness of wealth
shaped their psychological development.
Why others are wrong:
A focuses too narrowly on the character descriptions in the final paragraph rather than the core
thematic purpose.
B turns a personal observation about house size into a formal sociological evaluation.
D introduces an unmentioned argument regarding the unique superiority of a middle-class
upbringing.
Answer: B
Level: Moderate
Explanation: Reference Line: "At the age of seven... I was embarrassed when wealthier friends...
came over to my house, which was small, compared with theirs. Later... I felt the opposite: sheepish
about a house that was grander than some of my friends’ homes."
Why B is correct: The text shows that the author's discomfort was relative: they felt
embarrassed when their house was smaller compared to private school peers, but felt sheepish
when it was grander than public school peers. This indicates their social clocking of wealth relied
entirely on situational comparisons.
Why others are wrong:
A is a trap; the text implies the author's house size changed due to moving, but it does not state
that their family's underlying material conditions fluctuated wildly.
C attributes a specific preference for one school type over another that the author never states.
D invents an unmentioned struggle regarding maintaining friendships and mischaracterizes the
moves as economically forced.
10.	Answer: C
Level: Moderate
Explanation: Reference Line: "...as a patriarch who scandalised his WASPy beach club in
Southampton with his European Speedos, competed in every endeavour... and whom others craned
to impress, though he lived very privately."
Why C is correct: The passage describes the grandfather as someone who lived privately, yet
note that his competitive nature and individual choices (like the Speedos) drew attention and
made others "crane to impress" him, signaling a commanding but private presence.
Why others are wrong:
A contradicts the text's assertion that he lived "very privately."
B is incorrect because he "scandalised" his beach club, showing a departure from their established
cultural norms.
D introduces a business network and social leveraging narrative that is completely absent.

LAW PREP
— Tutorial—	MOCK CLAT 10028 : ANSWER & EXPLANATIONS
11.	Answer: B
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: "Though he’s now in his 90s, his shadow looms large — as a
patriarch who scandalised his WASPy beach club... and whom others craned to impress..."
Why B is correct: The phrase "shadow looms large" is a metaphor used to describe an individual
who possesses a lingering, powerful influence or presence over a group or family dynamic, even in
old age or absence.
Why others are wrong:
A treats the phrase as a literal physical or architectural description.
C claims the expression marks a failure or strain in memory, which is disproven by the vivid
recollections that follow.
D introduces unmentioned "private financial anxieties."
12.	Answer: A
Level: Moderate
Explanation: Reference Line: "House size was one of the earliest metrics by which I clocked
wealth."
Why A is correct: In this specific colloquial and reflective context, "clocked" functions as a verb
meaning to notice, register, calculate, or gauge. The presence of the word "metrics" anchors this,
showing that house size was used to measure or assess relative wealth.
Why others are wrong:
B implies the author was trying to control or govern wealth, which is contextually inaccurate.
C suggests the author was confronting or disputing wealth at that early stage, rather than simply
identifying it.
D relies on the mechanical speed-related definition of clocking ("to speed up"), which makes no
sense alongside the word "metrics."
13.	Answer: C
Level: Moderate
Explanation: Reference Line: "That’s the beauty of his art... the way it encourages the identity to
break down and dissolve in the face of its contemplation. In that sense, its underpinnings are not so
different from those of religious art...”
Why C is correct: The passage focuses on how looking at Rothko's abstract canvases produces a
spiritual, meditative experience characterized by the dissolving of the ego, which the author notes
shares the same underlying purpose as traditional religious art.
Why others are wrong:
A introduces an extreme judgment ("inherently superior") that the author never makes.
B claims the exhibition failed to replicate the environment, which is an unsupported negative
critique.
D uses absolute language ("completely dependent") and overstates the impact on Rothko's
background.

LAW PREP
— Tutorial—	MOCK CLAT 10028 : ANSWER & EXPLANATIONS
14.	Answer: A
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: ”...drawn there not by Michelangelo’s David or Botticelli’s Birth of
Venus, but by the works of Mark Rothko, that titan of US abstract expressionism whose work seems,
on the surface at least, distinctly secular and un-Florentine."
Why A is correct: The text explicitly notes that on the surface, Rothko's work seems "distinctly
secular and un-Florentine," allowing the reader to infer that the author recognized an initial
superficial mismatch between American abstraction and the classic Florentine setting.
Why others are wrong:
B overstates the author's personal context into "deep psychological distress."
C invents a value judgment regarding superiority that is absent from the text.
D directly contradicts the text, which states the author was not drawn there by Botticelli or
Michelangelo.
15.	Answer: B
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: (The progression of the narrative: Paragraph 1 establishes the
author's non-religious background; Paragraph 2 focuses on looking at the colors; Paragraph 3
discusses the breakdown of identity; Paragraph 4 notes the impact of Fra Angelico).
Why B is correct: The keywords seamlessly track the conceptual layers of the text: the author's
non-traditional background (Agnostic Spirituality), the method of viewing the large canvases
(Color-Field Contemplation), the resulting psychological effect (Ego Dissolution), and the
structural tie to classical masters (Renaissance Influence).
Why others are wrong:
A features "Artistic Rivalry," which is absent; Rothko was inspired by, not competing with, the
Renaissance.
C includes "Aesthetic Indifference" and "Emotional Detachment," both of which directly contradict
the author's tearful, highly emotional response.
D contains "Commercial Value," which is a theme completely untouched by the author.
16.	Answer: C
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: "As an unbaptised agnostic raised with no religion, the closest I
ever really come to a spiritual experience is when I’m standing in front of an artwork... [Rothko's
art] encourages the identity to break down... In that sense, its underpinnings are not so different
from those of religious art..."
Decoding the Question Stem: "Does not disagree with all... except" simplifies to: Which
statement does the author actually disagree with? (The author agrees with A, B, and D, but
disagrees with C).
Why C is correct: The author directly disproves this statement by using themselves as an
example: despite being an "unbaptised agnostic raised with no religion," they still experienced
deep spiritual, emotional vulnerability when looking at the art. Therefore, the author explicitly
disagrees with the idea that these feelings are dependent on a religious upbringing.
Why others are wrong:

LAW PREP
— Tutorial—	MOCK CLAT 10028 : ANSWER & EXPLANATIONS
A, B, and D are all claims that align perfectly with the author's arguments in the text. Because the
author agrees with them, they cannot be the correct "except" choice.
17.	Answer: B
Level: Moderate
Explanation: Reference Lines:
(For Statement 1): "...drawn there not by Michelangelo’s David or Botticelli’s Birth of Venus, but by
the works of Mark Rothko..."
(For Statement 2): "...the way it encourages the identity to break down and dissolve in the face of its
contemplation... I stopped thinking about myself at all."
(For Statement 3): "Yet seeing Renaissance art there had a profound impact on Rothko and his
painting... [he] wanted his own colour field paintings to provoke a similarly intense, spiritual
response."
Why B is correct: Only Statement 2 is true according to the passage. The text explicitly states
that Rothko's art causes the identity to dissolve and makes the author stop thinking about
themselves.
Why others are wrong:
Statement 1 is false because the author explicitly notes they were not drawn there by David.
Statement 3 is false because the text states that seeing Renaissance art had a "profound impact"
on Rothko and that he was "overwhelmed" by Fra Angelico's work, meaning he was far from
indifferent.
18.	Answer: A
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: "That’s the beauty of his art, especially in these self-referential
times: the way it encourages the identity to break down and dissolve in the face of its
contemplation."
Why A is correct: By setting up a contrast between our "self-referential times" (an era heavily
focused on the self/ego) and the capacity of Rothko's art to make a viewer "stop thinking about
myself at all," the author implies that the art serves as a crucial, refreshing antidote to modern
self-absorption.
Why others are wrong:
B shifts the focus to "modern art criticism" and "autobiographical context," which is an
unmentioned analytical framework.
C invents a historical claim about Rothko's era being insulated from dogma.
D uses overextended phrasing ("largely abandoned") to make an unsupported claim about the
habits of contemporary artists.
19.	Answer: A
Level: Moderate
Explanation: Reference Line: "While the series tends to use large-scale exhibitions as a cue, this
film spends only brief periods inside a gallery spaces..."

LAW PREP
— Tutorial—	MOCK CLAT 10028 : ANSWER & EXPLANATIONS
Why A is correct: By contrasting this specific film's choice to spend "only brief periods inside
gallery spaces" with the fact that the series normally uses "large-scale exhibitions as a cue," the
text implies that the typical entry in the series centers on physical gallery displays.
Why others are wrong:
B is a logical inversion; the text notes that academic talent and family members provide the
commentary here, but implies nothing about a lack of curators in other films.
C and D introduce overextended generalizations about the rest of the series' catalog that are
unsupported by the text.
20.	Answer: B
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: "Instead, we get a straightforward, meat-and-potatoes overview of
Kahlo’s life, peppered with copious commentary from the usual top-notch academic and curatorial
talent..."
Why B is correct: "Meat-and-potatoes" is a common idiom meaning basic, foundational, or no-
frills. The author uses it to describe a film that avoids flashy narrative tricks in favor of a clear,
standard chronological biography.
Why others are wrong: A takes the culinary phrase completely literally. C and D misinterpret
the phrase as a negative insult or an ironic critique, whereas the author explicitly calls the film
"very watchable" and notes that it efficiently "covers the required bases."
21.	Answer: B
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: (The overall structure of the passage, tracking its identity as a
review of a film that steps away from traditional gallery spaces to offer a "sober-toned" look at
Kahlo).
Why B is correct: This title captures the central structural element noted by the reviewer: the
fact that this specific film departs from the series' normal routine by spending "only brief periods
inside a gallery spaces" to focus on her personal history.
Why others are wrong: A overemphasizes the concept of reclaiming her, which is just a single
thematic goal mentioned in one paragraph. C isolates the retablo sidebar, which is a minor detail.
D focuses on a shared legacy, whereas the film is primarily a profile of Kahlo alone.
22.	Answer: A
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: (The sequence of sections: the film's format and style; its balance
of life and art; its attempt to look past "Fridamania"; and the discussion of her retablo influences).
Why A is correct: These terms capture the exact intellectual architecture of the passage: it
evaluates a film (Documentary Review), praises its distribution of personal and creative facts
(Biographical Balance), notes its tone relative to her popular hype (Phenomenon
Reclamation), and identifies what shaped her style (Aesthetic Influences).
Why others are wrong: B emphasizes "Marital Rivalry," which is not a theme explored in the
text. C labels the film a "Cinematic Failure," which completely contradicts the author's positive
conclusion. D mentions "Transatlantic Exhibitions," " an idea not present in this text.

LAW PREP
— Tutorial—	MOCK CLAT 10028 : ANSWER & EXPLANATIONS
23.	Answer: B
Level: Difficult
Explanation: Reference Line: "...Mexican retablo painting — the votive street art... which Kahlo
herself collected and which was a clear influence on her own work."
Decoding the Question Stem: "Does not disagree with all... except" simplifies to: Which
statement does the author actually disagree with? (The author agrees with A, C, and D, but
disagrees with B).
Why B is correct: The text explicitly notes that traditional Mexican retablo street art was "a
clear influence on her own work." Therefore, the author directly disagrees with the assertion that
her art was uninfluenced by these folk traditions.
Why others are wrong: A, C, and D are all claims that align perfectly with the factual
statements made by the reviewer. Because the author agrees with them, they cannot be the correct
"except" choice.
24.	Answer: A
Level: Moderate
Explanation: Reference Line: "Though necessarily a little light on detail, this is a film that
covers the required bases, striking a good balance between Kahlo’s often dramatic personal life and
the ins and outs of her artistic achievements.”
Why A is correct: By praising the film for achieving a "good balance" between her dramatic
biography and her concrete artistic accomplishments, the author implies that these two elements
are often in tension, and that biographical films run the risk of letting sensational personal drama
overshadow the actual art.
Why others are wrong: B is contradicted by the text, which shows her personal trauma (the
miscarriage) directly driving her artistic output. C and D introduce extreme or rigid claims that go
far beyond the reviewer's balanced commentary.
Current Affairs Including General Knowledge
25.	Answer: A
Explanation: Statement I is correct because the United Nations General Assembly designated 5
June as World Environment Day in 1972. This decision was linked with the 1972 Stockholm
Conference on the Human Environment, which was the first major global conference to place
environment at the centre of international discussion. Statement II is also correct because the first
World Environment Day celebration took place in 1973 with the slogan “Only One Earth.” The
slogan reflected the early global concern that environmental protection required common action by
all countries. Statement III is incorrect because World Environment Day did not originate from
the 1992 Rio Earth Summit. The Rio Earth Summit was important for sustainable development,
but World Environment Day had already been established two decades earlier. Hence, option (a) is
the correct answer.
26.	Answer: B
Explanation: Article 48A is a Directive Principle of State Policy. It directs the State to protect
and improve the environment and safeguard the forests and wildlife of the country. It was inserted
by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. Article 51A(g), on the other hand, is a

Fundamental Duty of citizens relating to environmental protection including forest, lakes, rivers
and wildlife. Therefore, Article 48A is the correct answer.
27.	Answer: C
Explanation: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 gives a broad definition of the
environment. It includes water, air and land, along with their interrelationship with human
beings, other living creatures, plants, micro-organisms and property. Therefore, it is incorrect to
say that the Act defines environment only in terms of forests and wildlife. The Act was enacted
after India’s participation in the 1972 Stockholm Conference and empowers the Central
Government to issue directions for environmental protection. Bhopal Gas Tragedy 1984 was also
one of the reason behind this act. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.
28.	Answer: C
Explanation: Principle 21 of the Stockholm Declaration balances two ideas: a State’s sovereign
right to exploit its own resources and its responsibility not to cause environmental damage beyond
its jurisdiction. This principle is widely treated as a foundational statement of the no-harm rule in
environmental law. Principle 24 deals more broadly with international cooperation. Hence,
Principle 21 is the correct answer.
29.	Answer: A
Explanation: India hosted the global World Environment Day celebration in 2018. The theme
that year was “Beat Plastic Pollution,” which focused on reducing plastic waste and single-use
plastic. World Environment Day 2026 was hosted by Azerbaijan, not India. The theme for the year
2026 is “Inspired by Nature. For Climate. For Our Future.” The first World Environment Day
celebration took place in 1973 and was not hosted by India.
The Rio Earth Summit was held in 1992, but World Environment Day had already been
established in 1972. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.
30.	Answer: C
Explanation: Nagpur City was listed under the High-Level Engagement category in the 50@50:
Cities Beating the Heat initiative. The initiative was linked with World Environment Day 2026
and focused on helping cities respond to extreme heat and climate-related urban risks. Mumbai
and Delhi were also associated with the wider initiative, but not under the High-Level
Engagement category. Therefore, Nagpur City is the correct answer.
31.	Answer: D
Explanation: World Environment Day 2026 used the campaign hashtag #NowForClimate.
The phrase reflected the urgency of climate action in a year marked by concern over heat,
emissions and climate risks. The campaign message focused on moving beyond delay and
strengthening collective action. #BeatPlasticPollution has been associated with plastic pollution
campaigns, especially in earlier World Environment Day themes. #OnlyOneEarth and
#GenerationRestoration are also linked with earlier environmental campaigns. Hence, option (d) is
the correct answer.

82.	Answer: C
Explanation: The exploration licence mechanism permits reconnaissance and prospecting
operations for deep-seated and critical minerals mentioned in the Seventh Schedule of the MMDR
Act. The reform was intended to attract specialised exploration agencies and private participation
in minerals such as lithium, cobalt, nickel, rare earth elements and tungsten. The First Schedule
is relevant for other statutory classifications, but the exploration licence is linked to the Seventh
Schedule. Hence, Option (c) is the correct answer.
33.	Answer: D
Explanation: Under the critical mineral policy framework, 24 critical minerals were included in
Part D of the First Schedule of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957.
This gives the Central Government the exclusive authority to auction mining leases and composite
licences for these specified minerals. The step is meant to strengthen national control over
strategically important mineral resources. These minerals are crucial for clean energy
technologies, batteries, electronics and strategic industries. District Mineral Foundations and
regulatory bodies have different functions, but they do not hold this auction authority for these
specified minerals. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.
34,	Answer: B
Explanation: Khanij Bidesh India Ltd, commonly known as KABIL, signed an Exploration and
Development contract with a state-owned company in Argentina. The agreement relates to lithium
blocks in Catamarca Province. Lithium is a key mineral for lithium-ion batteries, electric vehicles
and energy storage systems. This deal is part of India’s effort to secure overseas critical mineral
assets. Australia and Chile are also relevant to India’s critical mineral outreach, but the
Catamarca lithium project is associated with Argentina. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.
35.	Answer: D
Explanation: KABIL is a joint venture of National Aluminium Company Ltd., Hindustan Copper
Ltd. and Mineral Exploration and Consultancy Ltd in the ratio of 40 : 30 : 30. It was formed to
ensure supply-side assurance of critical and strategic minerals for India. Steel Authority of India
Limited is a major steel PSU, but it is not one of the three KABIL partners. Hence, Option (d) is
the correct answer.
36.	Answer: A
Explanation: Statement I is correct because the initiative was announced during the India-UK
Prime Ministers’ bilateral engagement in October 2025. Statement III is also correct because it
was later formalised through a Research Collaboration Agreement signed in March 2026.
Statement II is incorrect because the Observatory is not meant only for domestic coal mining
auctions. Its purpose is to monitor global critical mineral supply chains, identify risks and support
informed decisions. Therefore, the first and third statements are correct, while the second
statement is incorrect. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.
37.	Answer: C
Explanation: India’s 2023 list of 30 critical minerals includes minerals such as rhenium,
hafnium, tantalum, lithium, cobalt, graphite and rare earth elements. Uranium is not part of this

notified list of 30 critical minerals. This is relevant because India’s critical-mineral policy
separates many strategic minerals from atomic minerals and other regulatory categories. Hence,
Option (c) is the correct answer.
38.	Answer: C
Explanation: The National Waterways Act, 2016 created the statutory framework for India’s
national waterways system. It continued the first five National Waterways and declared 106
additional waterways, bringing the total to 111. This is relevant to blue-economy financing
because inland waterways support sustainable transport and port-linked logistics. Hence, Option
(c) is the correct answer.
39.	Answer: B
Explanation: Seychelles issued the world’s first sovereign blue bond in 2018. The bond raised
US$15 million and was supported by the World Bank and the Global Environment Facility. Its
proceeds were meant to support sustainable fisheries, marine conservation and ocean-based
economic activities. Seychelles was a suitable early issuer because it is an island nation whose
economy is closely linked with marine resources and the blue economy. Hence, option (b) is the
correct answer.
40.	Answer: C
Explanation: The Indian Ocean Rim Association is an intergovernmental organisation for
cooperation among Indian Ocean littoral states. Its Secretariat is located at Ebene in Mauritius.
Blue Economy is one of IORA’s important cross-cutting areas, making the grouping relevant to
ocean-based financing, fisheries, ports, shipping and marine-resource governance. Hence, Option
(c) is the correct answer.
41.	Answer: B
Explanation: Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited is preparing to issue India’s first blue
bond. It is a maritime-focused lender linked with India’s port, shipping and blue economy sectors.
The proposed bond is important because it expands India’s sustainable finance market beyond
conventional green bonds. The funds are expected to support maritime and coastal infrastructure.
NABARD, SIDBI and IREDA are important financial institutions, but they are not the proposed
issuer of India’s first blue bond. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.
42.	Answer: C
Explanation: The proposed blue bond structure includes a 7500 crore greenshoe option.
A greenshoe option allows the issuer to raise an additional amount when investor demand is
strong. It gives flexibility to expand the issue beyond the base amount. In this case, the base issue
is %500 crore and the greenshoe option is another %500 crore. Together, they make the total
proposed fund-raising size up to =1,000 crore. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.
43.	Answer: C
Explanation: In April 2026, the Government reconstituted NITI Aayog and appointed Ashok
Kumar Lahiri as its Vice Chairperson. He succeeded Suman K. Bery in that position. The

LAW PREP

reconstitution also included the appointment of several full-time members, including Rajiv Gauba
and others. Arvind Panagariya was the first Vice Chairperson of NITI Aayog, but he was not
appointed in the 2026 reconstitution. Hence, option (c) is correct.
44,	Answer: B
Explanation: The Aspirational Districts Programme was launched in January 2018 by the Prime
Minister. It aims to quickly and effectively transform 112 under-developed districts across India.
The programme is based on convergence of schemes, collaboration between different levels of
government, and competition among districts through data-based ranking. The figure of 500 is
closer to the Aspirational Blocks Programme as originally launched, not the Aspirational Districts
Programme. Therefore, option (b) is correct.
45.	Answer: A
Explanation: Atal Innovation Mission is an initiative under NITI Aayog to promote innovation
and entrepreneurship. It supports innovation through mechanisms such as Atal Tinkering Labs
and Atal Incubation Centres. The initiative is linked with building a culture of problem-solving
among students, start-ups and institutions. It is not a judicial digitisation scheme, a fintech
regulation framework or a defence infrastructure project. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.
46.	Answer: B
Explanation: The 11th Governing Council Meeting of NITI Aayog was held on the theme
“Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047”. The theme focused on improving human
development outcomes across age, gender, region and socio-economic groups. It was aligned with
the wider national vision of making India a developed country by 2047. Option (a) is close to the
theme of the 10th Governing Council Meeting held in 2025, but it is not the theme of the 11th
meeting. Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.
47.	Answer: A
Explanation: SIPRI stands for Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.
It is an independent international institute based in Sweden.
Its work focuses on conflict, armaments, arms control and disarmament.
SIPRI is widely known for its annual Yearbook and defence-related databases.
The other options are not the official expansion of SIPRI.
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.
48.	Answer: B
Explanation: New START was signed by the United States and Russia in Prague in April 2010.
It entered into force in February 2011 and placed limits on deployed strategic nuclear warheads
